title: Turkey name World Cup squad: What U.S. should expect from Group D opponents
content:
Turkey have named their 26-man squad for the 2026 men’s World Cup ahead of their first tournament appearance in nearly a quarter-century.

As expected, leading their World Cup roster are Real Madrid star Arda Güler, Juventus forward Kenan Yıldız and Inter Milan captain Hakan Çalhanoğlu, who arrives in the United States fresh off a second Scudetto with the Italian team.

Following a dramatic playoff campaign — on brand for the country that exports some of the best soap operas of the last decade — which saw them beat Romania in the semifinals and Kosovo in their final, Turkey secured one of Europe’s final four qualification spots, marking just their third World Cup appearance and their first since their historic third-place finish in 2002.

Turkey beat Macedonia 4-0 on June 1 in Istanbul before taking on Venezuela at Chase Stadium in Fort Lauderdale, Florida on June 6.

They will play Australia on June 14 to begin their tournament in Vancouver before taking on Paraguay on June 19 and co-hosts the United States on June 25 to round off Group D.

The Turks have already shown they can trouble the hosts. In a June 2025 friendly, Turkey came from behind to beat Mauricio Pochettino’s side 2-1, overcoming an early Jack McGlynn goal through strikes from Arda Güler and Kerem Aktürkoğlu.

This Turkey squad may be even more talented than the generation that captivated the world under Şenol Güneş 24 years ago. Turkey is arguably the most dangerous threat to the USMNT’s hopes of topping the group. Armed with a blend of emerging European stars and top players from the Turkish Super League, they possess the talent, experience and confidence to challenge the hosts in what could be the defining match of the group stage.

Madrid’s Güler has emerged as one of Europe’s most exciting young playmakers, capping a breakthrough season by earning UEFA Champions League Young Player of the Season honors. Yıldız, meanwhile, has quickly become one of Juve’s most dangerous attacking threats, with the 21-year-old already drawing comparisons to club icon Alessandro Del Piero.

Then there is Çalhanoğlu, the veteran captain whose vision, passing range and dead-ball expertise continue to anchor head coach Vincenzo Montella’s midfield.

Together, the trio has inspired hopes that Turkey can write the next great chapter in the nation’s football history, following in the footsteps of the 2002 side that captured the world’s imagination with an unlikely run to the semifinals.

Turkey will travel to the U.S. on the back of a convincing 4-0 victory over North Macedonia, an opponent Montella chose because of their similarities to Australia.

During the match, Montella rotated heavily, making 11 changes as he evaluated his final World Cup options. Speaking before the fixture, Montella said he wanted to assess players who had seen limited minutes at club level while also managing those carrying minor injuries. He revealed that he would submit his final World Cup squad list before the final whistle at Chobani Stadium in Istanbul, home of Fenerbahçe.

“Honestly, every player deserves to be here,” Montella said. “That’s why it was a very difficult day for me. It was an emotional day. Making the final decisions is never easy. It’s difficult for the players as well. I experienced it myself when I was a player.”

Since taking charge, the Italian manager has sought to bring greater tactical discipline and composure to a national team that has often struggled for consistency since its golden run at the 2002 World Cup.

Under Montella, Turkey had a promising Euros performance in 2024, finishing fifth. With Güler emerging as the face of a generation many supporters believe could become the country’s strongest in decades.

Goalkeepers: Altay Bayındır (Manchester United), Mert Günok (Fenerbahçe), Uğurcan Çakır (Galatasaray).

Defenders: Abdülkerim Bardakcı (Galatasaray), Çağlar Söyüncü (Fenerbahçe), Eren Elmalı (Galatasaray), Ferdi Kadıoğlu (Brighton & Hove Albion), Merih Demiral (Al Ahli), Mert Müldür (Fenerbahçe), Ozan Kabak (Hoffenheim), Samet Akaydın (Çaykur Rizespor), Zeki Çelik (AS Roma).

Midfielders: Hakan Çalhanoğlu (Inter), İsmail Yüksek (Fenerbahçe), Kaan Ayhan (Galatasaray), Orkun Kökçü (Beşiktaş), Salih Özcan (Borussia Dortmund).

Forwards: Arda Güler (Real Madrid), Barış Alper Yılmaz (Galatasaray), Can Uzun (Eintracht Frankfurt), Deniz Gül (FC Porto), İrfan Can Kahveci (Kasımpaşa), Kenan Yıldız (Juventus), Kerem Aktürkoğlu (Fenerbahçe), Oğuz Aydın (Fenerbahçe), Yunus Akgün (Galatasaray).
